avertissement: The definitions in this glossary are written by DossierNBrunswick — they are not the City of Fredericton’s texts nor legal definitions. What comes from the minutes is the count of occurrences and the example under each term.

entrees.definition: The Mayor and twelve Councillors, one per ward, elected for four years. Council decides by resolution: a member moves it, another seconds it, and Council carries or defeats it.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: The meeting type on every card.

entrees.definition: A Council meeting held on the regular schedule, usually on Monday evening every two weeks.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: Most meetings in the period.

entrees.definition: A Council meeting called outside the regular schedule, for one stated purpose, such as the swearing-in of a new Council.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: The minutes open with the purpose of the meeting.

entrees.definition: A Councillor chosen by Council to act for the Mayor when the Mayor is away.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: Council appoints the Deputy Mayor by resolution.

entrees.definition: Part of a meeting held without the public, for matters the law allows to be kept private, such as land deals or legal advice. Any decision is then voted on in public.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: Cards marked “From the … Closed Session”.

exemple.objet: Specialized Police Services Agreements – City of Edmundston and Town of Woodstock (From the November 9, 2026 Closed Session)

entrees.definition: All members of Council sitting as a committee to study a matter before Council decides it.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: Under “Council-in-Committee Reports” in the minutes.

entrees.definition: The member who puts a resolution forward, and the member who supports putting it to a vote. Neither tells you how the others voted.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: On every card.

entrees.definition: The resolution was adopted. Fredericton’s minutes do not say by how many votes, nor who voted against.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: The result on almost every card.

entrees.definition: The resolution was rejected.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: The result on a card, when it happens.

exemple.objet: Defers consideration of the Report of the Expropriations Advisory Officer received on May 8, 2026, and the…

entrees.definition: A member with a personal interest in an item declares it at the start of the meeting and takes no part in that item.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: Under “Conflict of Interest Declarations” in the minutes.

entrees.definition: A resolution by which Council excuses a member’s absence from a meeting.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: Near the end of some meetings.

entrees.definition: A group of routine items adopted together, in a single resolution. Any member can ask for an item to be taken out and voted on separately.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: One card per meeting, with every item it covers in the text.

entrees.definition: A municipal law adopted by Council. Each one has a letter and a number: Z for zoning, T for traffic, and so on.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: Cards titled “By-law No. …”.

exemple.objet: By-law No. Z-6.15 - Redesignate Land to permit the subdivision of an unserviced lot at 575 Highland Avenue- Municipal Plan Amendment

entrees.definition: A by-law is read three times before it takes effect. Council often gives first and second reading at one meeting and third reading at a later one.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: The same by-law comes back on several cards, a few weeks apart.

exemple.objet: By-law No. Z-5.376 – 140-146 Wallace Avenue – Rezoning (Harvona Contracting Inc.)

entrees.definition: Instead of reading a by-law out in full, Council reads a summary of it, as the Local Governance Act allows.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: A card just before the third reading of a by-law.

exemple.objet: By-law No. Z-5.375 – 148-152 Clark Street– Rezoning (City of Fredericton)

entrees.definition: The first resolution of a meeting: Council adopts its agenda, sometimes with items added.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: The first card of each meeting.

entrees.definition: Council adopts the minutes of an earlier meeting. They become the official record only then.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: Cards titled “Minutes of the … Meeting”.

exemple.objet: Minutes of the Regular Meeting of City Council - August 24, 2026

entrees.definition: A change to the zoning by-law (Z-5) that sets what can be built on a property.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: Cards titled “By-law No. Z-5.… – Rezoning”.

exemple.objet: By-law No. Z-5.376 – 140-146 Wallace Avenue – Rezoning (Harvona Contracting Inc.)

entrees.definition: Before deciding a rezoning, Council hears anyone who wishes to speak. The Mayor then closes the hearing and Council votes.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: The second reading of a zoning by-law.

entrees.definition: Conditions Council attaches to a rezoning under section 59 of the Community Planning Act, which the owner must meet.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: A card in the series of each rezoning.

exemple.objet: Change to Terms and Conditions – 269 Two Nations Crossing (12 Neighbours Community Inc.) A change in Terms and Conditions, pertaining to By-law No. Z-5.241

entrees.definition: The number that identifies a piece of land in Service New Brunswick’s registry.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: Land purchases, sales and exchanges.

exemple.objet: 447-449 Northumberland Street (PID 01440650) - Tentative Plan of Subdivision (Christopher Thomas)

entrees.definition: An agreement under which another government pays part of a City project.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: Cards on grants from the province or from Ottawa.

exemple.objet: Municipal Capital Borrowing Board Funding – Pumper Tanker, Fire Services (From the October 26, 2026 Closed Session)

entrees.definition: The City buys, sells or exchanges land. Council authorizes the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign the documents.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: Cards on land and buildings.

exemple.objet: Acquisition of Route 105 PID 75136788 by Donation
